paper.version: React. Chem. Eng., 2016, 1, 658-666 (open access PMC5123644, CC BY 3.0)
paper.title: Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling optimization enabled by automated feedback
paper.goal: maximize TON subject to reaction yield > 90 % of the maximum yield (Table 1 case I: yield 82 %, TON 69)

code.model: summit.benchmarks.get_pretrained_reizman_suzuki_emulator(case=2): 5-ANN ensemble mean, clip=True; catalysts addressed by public names (worker SUMMIT_CATALYSTS)

license.data: CSV and weights ship in the MIT-licensed Summit repo; original measurements from Reizman et al. 2016

metrics.name: yield
metrics.transform: identity (%); ensemble mean of 5 ANNs, clipped to [0, 100]

metrics.name: ton
metrics.transform: derived (U13/U22): yield(%) / catalyst_loading(mol%); the ANN's own TON output is not used

hidden_criteria.rule: TON within 2 % of the best TON this reactor model reaches while keeping yield >= 38.08 % (the evaluator holds that TON value; it is not given to you)

success_rule.paper_goal_mapping: U44: the paper's goal (maximize TON subject to a high-yield constraint) made strict on the emulator: yield >= 95 % of the emulator's grid-max yield (public 38.08); TON >= 98 % of the best derived TON on the 54,264-point grid under that constraint (evaluator-held); 1 grid points succeed. Difficulty checked against an informed heuristic without the loading hint (median 17-40 experiments across cases), not against random search.

near_target_residual.definition: data rows whose OBSERVED values meet the public success rule

notes: U24 accepted limitation: held-out validation error unavailable (upstream stores no train/test split); error vs the CSV includes training rows.

U24 accepted limitation: paper/CSV calibration mismatch (CSV rows near the paper optimum can exceed Table 1); success is defined on the emulator's own outputs, results are a within-simulator comparison.
U24 accepted limitation: completeness of failure records in the CSV not verified; the emulator never fails an experiment.
U23: public text names the substrates, the fixed base/solvent and the precatalysts by commercial names; the paper's codes are mapped only inside the worker.

Worker env .envs/summit: CPython 3.10.20, torch 1.13.1 (CPU), skorch 0.11.0, scikit-learn 1.2.1, pandas 1.5.3, scipy 1.10.0, numpy 1.23.5. Upstream poetry.lock pins numpy 1.22.4, which is ABI-incompatible with the torch 1.13.1 wheel ('module compiled against API version 0x10'); 1.23.5 satisfies upstream's numpy ^1.21.
Upstream code unmodified; the clone is imported via sys.path (not installed).
U44 known success inputs: every grid point meeting the public yield threshold and the hidden TON threshold (1).
